key_insight: Embedding an asymptotic boundary-layer corrector in neural trial functions preserves accuracy at small viscosity without requiring a grid that resolves the layer.
engineering_relevance: The approach could reduce training costs for low-viscosity flow simulation by representing thin wall layers analytically rather than resolving them numerically.
method: Use the 2D incompressible Navier–Stokes vorticity–stream function formulation with slip boundary conditions.
Embed a corrector for the √ε-wide vorticity layer, tying its amplitude to the network’s wall trace without knowing the limit solution.
Replace the residual Laplacian with coarse-grid finite-volume flux differences to obtain sl-FVNN.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports viscosity-uniform error over six decades for Stokes and Navier–Stokes tests, with sl-FVNN matching sl-PINN accuracy within random-seed scatter at about half the training-step cost.
watch_item: The reported results concern 2D flows with slip boundaries; extension to other boundary conditions or geometries requires validation.
paper_title: Singular layer neural networks for the Navier-Stokes equations at small viscosity
